A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LightReasoner and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite extensive reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, expert–amateur pairing experiments, component ablations, and reasoning case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds sampling-length experiments and evaluations on three commonsense benchmarks.

M1.justification: The method retains KL-based step selection, masked expert–amateur contrastive targets, and forward-KL self-distillation with LoRA. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix without changing its procedure; the new explanations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds CommonsenseQA, HellaSwag, and ARC-Challenge evaluations for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B in Appendix G.2/Table 8. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained mathematical and STEM benchmarks into commonsense reasoning. Training remains based on GSM8K.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same baseline models, rejection-sampled SFT, ground-truth supervision, and ablation variants. Table 6 merely renames SFT as Rejection SFT. Newly discussed self-distillation methods are not experimentally evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix G.1 introduces a controlled experiment varying sampling caps across 64, 128, and 256 tokens. The existing experiments retain the 128-token default, 1000 training steps, masking/filtering thresholds, and evaluation prompting arrangements.

E4.justification: The new truncation-length study tests whether performance depends on the sampling prefix length. Existing component ablations, filtering analysis, convergence curves, and all ten case studies are retained; referencing those cases as evidence against shallow reasoning does not add new cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's new discussion of sampling as variance reduction is a conceptual mechanism explanation, not a new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports baseline/LightReasoner scores of 62.6/64.2 on CommonsenseQA, 46.2/47.4 on HellaSwag, and 42.8/45.6 on ARC-Challenge. Table 7 adds results at 64 and 256 sampling tokens. These expand the reported findings substantially; the corresponding original performance, efficiency, pairing, and ablation tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical content in v1 Appendices B–E matches v2 Appendices C–F. Expanded chain-rule steps, expectation notation, and naming the existing contrastive weight as an advantage restate the same mathematics. The added noise-reduction explanation supplies no new formal assumptions or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion add the explicit qualification that matching or surpassing SFT holds under equal experimental settings. The central expert–amateur contribution and headline accuracy and resource-saving claims remain unchanged, making this a limited qualification of the comparative claim.

C2.justification: New Section 3.1.3 acknowledges that shared incorrect reasoning can produce misleading high-KL supervision and explains the intended mitigations. v2 also adds explicit limitations concerning domain coverage, pairing, hyperparameters, and scale, plus substantive interpretations of noise reduction, truncation sensitivity, and commonsense transfer.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 documents the tested token caps and procedural details for the new truncation control. Existing hardware, precision, LoRA settings, learning rates, prompt templates, and repository link are retained, with the detailed implementation appendix moving from F to H.

R1.justification: Appendix A replaces the broad post-training overview with substantial discussions of selective-token training and self-distillation, including SDFT, SDPO, and Self-Distilled Reasoner. It positions LightReasoner against privileged-context and on-policy approaches, removes several earlier general post-training references, and drops the categorical claim to be first to use model contrast during training.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes widespread condensation and rewriting. Related work is reorganized, Design Rationale and Limitations sections are added, the standalone Reproducibility section and appendix contents page disappear, and the appendices are reorganized around new experiments and an LLM-writing disclosure.

P2.justification: Most of the document changes from one column to two columns, substantially rearranging figures and tables. Figure 1 changes from a horizontal strip to a 2-by-2 arrangement, Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix, and two result tables are added. Existing plots and case studies are largely redisplayed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves the paper through broader empirical coverage, a truncation control, explicit failure conditions, and more focused research positioning. The gains remain limited: the new evaluations lack detailed protocols and uncertainty estimates, and Table 7's substantial score variation does not establish the claimed insensitivity to truncation length. The central method and main experimental evidence remain unchanged.
